rv.q: It is a work of considerable intelligence and emotional force—one that grips, disturbs, and compels in equal measure.
Peter Coleman’s take on Joseph Goebbels, one of history’s most horrifying characters, is quite forgettable.

cn.t: James Clements' intricate examination of Leni Riefenstahl draws mixed reactions—one critic praises its bracing precision in exploring artistic genius and moral complicity, while another finds the production less compelling in its historical exploration.
